summary: Jiro Kawakita was a scholar of Tibetology who studied at Kyoto University (~1939–1943). He held posts at the Tokyo Institute of Technology (~1960–1977), the University of Tsukuba (~1978–1985), and Chubu University (~1985–1993).

Jiro Murata was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Sinology. He studied at Kyoto University (~1917–1920) and later held a post at the National Institute of Technology, Akashi College (~1962–1968).

Jiro Sugiyama worked in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. After studying at the University of Tokyo (~1950–1953), he held posts at Tokyo National Museum (~1957–1987), Nagaoka University of Technology (~1987–1993), International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies (~1996–2004), and Bukkyo University.
Jiryo Masuda worked in Buddhist studies and Indology, studying under Unrai Wogihara (attested 1930). He later served as a professor at the University of Calcutta.

Jitendra Nath Banerjea specialized in Indology, history, and archaeology. He studied under Hemchandra Raychaudhuri and served as Carmichael Professor of Ancient Indian History and Culture at the University of Calcutta (~1918–1959).

Jitendra Nath Mohanty was an Indology and philosophy scholar who studied at Presidency University, University of Calcutta, and University of Göttingen. He taught at Calcutta, Burdwan, The New School, University of Oklahoma, Emory University, and Temple University (~1986–2003).
Jitsushyu Oshika is a scholar in Indology and Buddhist studies who studied at Tohoku University. He later served as a professor at Toyo University (attested 1980–1981).

Jitsuzo Kuwabara studied Sinology, history, and archaeology at the University of Tokyo (~1893–1896). He subsequently held posts at Third Higher School (1898–1899), Tokyo Higher Normal School (1899–1907), and Kyoto Imperial University (1909–1930).
Jiun Kubota is a scholar of Buddhist studies and religious studies who studied under Kōun Yamada (~1970–1985) and eventually succeeded him.

Jiyu Ren studied philosophy, religious studies, and Buddhist studies at Peking University under Yongtong Tang and Lin He. He held posts at Peking University, the Chinese Academy of Sciences, the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences, and the National Library of China.

Jiyu-Kennett was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Trinity Laban Conservatoire, Durham University, and Soji-ji under Seck Kim Seng, Keidō Chisan Kōho, and Suigan Yogo. She served as head priest at Unpuku-ji and abbess of Shasta Abbey (~1970–1996).

Joachim Gentz is a scholar of Sinology and religious studies. He has held posts as Junior Professor in Religious Studies at the University of Göttingen and Reader in Chinese Studies at the University of Edinburgh (attested 2013).
Joachim Heinrich Campe was a scholar in linguistics and other fields who studied at the University of Helmstedt (~1765–1768) and Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg (~1768–1769).
Joachim Prandstetter studied Indology and philosophy at the University of Vienna (graduating in 1994), where he studied under Gerhard Oberhammer.

Joachim Wach studied religious studies and philosophy across Leipzig, Heidelberg, Munich, Berlin, Freiburg, Freiberg, and Leiden. He taught at Leipzig University (1924–1935), Brown University (1935–1946), and University of Chicago Divinity School (1945–1955).

Joan Jiko Halifax studied at Tulane, Newcomb College, Miami, and Union Institute & University, training under Seungsahn Haengwon and Bernie Glassman. She held posts at Columbia, Musée de l'Homme, Miller School of Medicine, Maryland Psychiatric Research Center, and Harvard.

Joanna Gottfried Williams was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. She studied at Swarthmore College, Radcliffe College, and Harvard University before serving as a professor at the University of California, Berkeley (~1971–2003).
Joanna Macy is a scholar of Buddhist studies and religious studies who studied at Wellesley College (~1946–1950) and Syracuse University (~1973–1978).

Joanne Punzo Waghorne, a scholar of religious studies and Indology, studied at the University of Chicago. She held posts at the University of Massachusetts Boston, Bowdoin College, the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill, and Syracuse University.

Joe Bransford Wilson studied Buddhist studies and Tibetology at Wisconsin-Madison and Virginia under teachers including Geshe Lhundub Sopa and Lati Rinpoche. He taught at the University of Virginia (1981–1985) and UNC Wilmington (attested 1994–2001).
